projects.name: Capacity building activities and training programmes aimed at strengthening criminal justice response to organized crime and enhancement of the international cooperation skills
projects.description:
UNODC technical assistance in Turkmenistan for the 2021-2025 period strategically pivoted to strengthening institutional capacities. UNODC placed significant emphasis on strengthening the operational and procedural competencies of law enforcement agencies and the judiciary to combat transnational threats and organized crime. This comprehensive support targeted the full spectrum of action, specifically enhancing national capacities for the detection, investigation, prosecution, and adjudication of organized crime, trafficking in illicit goods and drugs, corruption, and terrorism in line with international standards and best practices.

A core component of this work was dedicated to building robust capacities in evidence collection and investigative techniques, including trainings in Open-Source Intelligence methodologies. Furthermore, UNODC assistance actively facilitated and strengthened international cooperation, providing critical support for effective mutual legal assistance in cross-border cases. Through tailored workshops, simulation exercises, Mock-trials and the provision of practical guideline materials, UNODC equipped criminal justice practitioners and frontline professionals with the advanced skills and knowledge necessary to navigate complex, modern criminal investigations, thereby fortifying the entire chain of justice and enhancing international collaborative efforts.

projects.name: Integrated natural resources management in drought-prone and salt-affected agricultural production landscapes
projects.description: The overall objective of the project "Integrated natural resources management in drought-prone and salt-affected agricultural production landscapes " is to scale up integrated natural resources management (INRM) in drought prone and salt affected agricultural production landscapes in the Central Asian countries and Turkey. This will be done through scaling up of sustainable management practices that minimize pressures and negative impacts on natural resources that reduce risks and vulnerability and, enhance capacity of rural communities to cope with or adapt to drought and salinity. In particular, adoption of integrated landscape management approaches and INRM practices should help stabilize and even reverse trends of soil salinization, reduce erosion, improve water capture and retention, increase the sequestration of carbon, and reduce loss of agrobiodiversity, thereby reducing the desertification trend in terms of extent and severity. The project objective will be achieved during a five-year period through four project components. It is structured as a program with one multi-country component addressing shared priorities at multi-county level (Component 1), two components at national level ensuring national implementation in selected production landscapes/land use systems (Component 2 and Component 3), and one M&E component (Component 4). The needs of disadvantaged groups, gender and age issues will be given consideration throughout the Project’s implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and are reflected in the Project design.

projects.name: Enhancing Capacities for Climate-Resilient Water Management and Catalysing Nature-Positive transformation of agriculture in Turkmenistan for enhanced resilience
projects.description:
The project "Enhancing Capacities for Climate-Resilient Water Management " aims to address these gaps by integrating the economic assessment of natural capital into climate-resilient water management practices. Building upon Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) approaches, the project will enhance institutional capacity to develop net-zero pathways and long-term strategies in the agricultural sector, while strengthening the capacity of local government and farmers. By focusing on the value of natural capital, the project will emphasize the economic benefits of sustainable water management, thereby justifying incentives for behavioral change towards these practices.
Moreover, this project aims to improve the capacity of stakeholders to enhance carbon sinks in agricultural land and enhance carbon sequestration in communities through NbS at natural ecosystem levels. By developing a novel methodology for the economic assessment of natural capital and applying it in water management, the project will contribute to more resilient communities and ecosystems in Turkmenistan.

The project will achieve environmental benefits as increased climate change resilience, Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN), increased Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), decrease in Green House Gas (GHG) emissions by addressing both the drivers of land degradation and biodiversity loss, enhancing their synergies and reinforcing the links between CBD, UNFCCC and the UNCCD. The two key elements of the project are: (1) the soft component with a focus on the promotion of climate change adaptation at local level, as well as of the long-term strategies at the institutional level, and (2) the hard components, leveraging the NbS and IWRM under the strategies to enhance carbon sinks, conserve high-carbon ecosystems and decrease non-CO2 emissions, while simultaneously increasing farmer resilience.

projects.name: Improving adaptive capacity and resilience of local communities to climate change induced water shortages and land degradation in two climate affected regions of Turkmenistan
projects.description: Turkmenistan with its highly arid climate and scarce water resources is particularly vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change. The adverse effects of climate change, such as water shortages and land degradation, contribute to economic decline and job loss in the agricultural sector, serving as a push factor of migration from the primary sector dependent regions of Turkmenistan, mainly Dashoguz and Lebap. In these regions, land degradation and shortage of irrigation water for agriculture affect agricultural productivity and, accordingly, quality of life of the local communities, forcing them to migrate. However, for some vulnerable groups, primarily families of migrants left behind and women-led households, migration is not an option because they do not have economic and other resources. In this regard, the project will prioritize adaptation in-situ to build resilience of these vulnerable groups and promote their climate resilient development through demonstration of the efficient use of water resources, use of innovative “green” technologies in land and water use, water-smart practices for greater access to safe drinking water and irrigation, raising public awareness to encourage responsible water consumption, promoting stakeholder interaction and cooperation for better adaptation planning at the local level, and enhancing the knowledge and capacity of targeted vulnerable groups as well as local administrations through education and training.

projects.description:
The hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFC) phase-out management plan (HPMP) was developed to enable Turkmenistan to meet its obligations under the Montreal Protocol and its amendments. The plan was prepared in close cooperation with the Government of Turkmenistan by the National Ozone Unit, the United Nations Industrial Development Organization and the United Nations Environment Programme. It was formulated in accordance with the processes and guidance set out in relevant decisions of the Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol and the Executive Committee of the Multilateral Fund.

The HPMP for Turkmenistan is implemented through a combination of investment and non-investment activities, structured in two stages and focused on the refrigeration and air-conditioning servicing sector. Stage I, implemented over a five-year period, aimed to achieve HCFC consumption reductions of 10% by 2015 and 35% by 2020. Stage II, covering the period from 2020 to 2040, is designed to achieve the complete phase-out of HCFCs, reaching a 100% reduction in consumption.

The second output is that national capacities will be strengthened by improving and updating knowledge and techniques (Training-of-Trainers, exposure visits) and by making available practical guidelines on different locust issues. Under the third output, locust monitoring will be improved thanks to the delivery of transportation means, positioning, communication and survey equipment as well as the introduction and/or support provided for the use of the Automated System for Data Collection (ASDC) and national Geographical Information System (GIS) named “Caucasus and Central Asia Locust Management System (CCALM)”, allowing collection and analysis of standardized field locust data. The fourth output is that locust control operations will be supported thanks to the delivery of vehicles, tractors and sprayers of different modifications; alternatives to conventional pesticides such as Insect Growth Regulators and biopesticides will also be promoted. The fifth output concerns risk reduction for human health and the environment: this will include mitigating impact of locust control operations on human health and the environment through delivery of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), a pilot activity on empty containers management and preparing extension documentation for local staff; it will also comprise the monitoring of impact of locust control operations through supporting Human Health and Environment Monitoring Teams and delivering health and environment monitoring equipment. The last and sixth input aims at developing awareness of the local populations and decision-makers to locust issues by producing informational, communication and advocacy materials. The project will focus on the provinces that are the most affected by locusts in the six Central Asian countries.
